item.title: Re: Author Commentary
item.content:encoded:
Sorta close.

Every sapient being has the potential to be Wondertainment. Most who show up are on the low end of the spectrum, and thus while wonderful, don't do much anomalous at all. Their form of magic is rather mundane.

But then you get people like Reggie, who have The Stuff. Now, everyone has a little bit of The Stuff. It's like Spiral Power. Erryone has it, but some people have it, you know? This is where things get magical.

As far as the title of Wondertainment is concerned, the number and spread is uncertain, mostly to allow for a certain fluidity of both character and timeline, so that other people can have valid Wondertainments. This is just for those individuals who claim the name, though, there are a great many who do not. 'Familial relations' of the Wondertainments are not genetic.

Weird Al is a Wondertainment. It is known.

item.title: Re: Author Commentary
item.content:encoded:
I believe the way it works is that Wondertainments have existed since ye olden days of the Djoricverse, and are basically the physical manifestations of humanity's creativity (although they probably went under a different label before Reginald came up with the name), teaching cavemen the secret of fire (see AiC) and otherwise guiding along humanity with their insights. People who fit the role of a Wondertainment would be granted all the powers and privileges that a Wondertainment possessed (although the selection process evidently isn't flawless, as shown by Reginald here joining the Factory, which is pretty much the antithesis of Wondertainment and everything they stand for.) However, no Wondertainment thus far has managed to unlocked their true potential; how that is done, what advantages come with that, and other such details I leave for Djoric to explore in the future.
Feel free to correct me if I'm wrong, as always.

item.title: Author Commentary
item.content:encoded:
To jumpstart some actual discussion on the tale, I'm going to drop my thoughts on it.

+ Spoilers ahoy
- Spoilers away

This was something of a spur of the moment tale, though the ideas behind it have been around it for a while now.

Blackwood, Wondertainment, and Mr. Dark were drinking buddies at the pub called the Green Hart in the 1860s. The group split up: Blackwood founded his adventurers and began to work for the crown, and that led to the formation of the English parent of the Foundation. Dark did his own thing, and Wondy tried to make toys.

Dr. Wondertainment is, of course, not his real name: it's something he made up when introducing his toys at the 1893 World's Fair. His actual name (mentioned, if exaggerated, in "Assistance for the Boss Lady") is Reginald Westinghouse. He wasn't able to sell many of his ideas on his own, so he ended up doing concept design for the Factory.

It broke him, and while he escaped his contract, the damage to his mind was not something he could recover from. He made up the Wondertainment persona, devoted himself again to making toys, and had some moderate success (non-anomalous, even)

Eventually, his normal toys were replaced with the anomalous ones, at around the same time that he began realizing that there was something off about him, and that there were other Wondertainments out there. We see him here having, unsuccessfully, merged their minds into his (and in some cases, their bodies: those stitches weren't just for show) in an attempt to access the full spectrum of Wondertainment memories.

His attempts to create an heir that would be able to possess all of those memories and experiences and powers from the beginning were all failures. Most never had anything, and were ruined physically or mentally besides. Mr. Redd did have access to a lot of the legacy, but he was insane (possibly even SK-connected). That bit was, of course, a little allusion to Cool War, though only a little bit.

Now, we have seen Isabel gain an awareness of the Wondertainment legacy, so it seems that her father's despair was not entirely correct. But the matter of how, and why, she gained that knowledge, and Emma's place in the scheme, still remains to be seen.
